title: Quarterly Private Deployment Initiative Bucketing, Milestones & Go/No-Go Criteria
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Purpose: Convert high-level OKRs for Private/VPC/On‑Prem into a prioritized, timeboxed quarterly plan. This ticket captures initiative bucketing (core platform, security/compliance, customer enablement), milestone sequencing, explicit go/no-go criteria per milestone, and a communications/handoff plan. The outcome will be a single-page quarterly playbook that engineering and GTM can commit to and operate from.

Scope: All features required to meet enterprise SLAs and compliance checklists for Private deployments in Q3: network integration templates (VPC peering, private link), upgrade tooling for on-prem connectors, KMS/HSM integration path, tenant isolation audits, and on-prem installation reproducibility. Excludes longer-term platform refactors not schedulable this quarter (these will be captured in the backlog with owners).

Why now: Multiple inbound enterprise deals require guaranteed upgrade windows, audit logs, and key management support before end of Q3; sales and solutions engineering have flagged several at‑risk customers without clear delivery commitments. This plan reduces ambiguity and defines measurable acceptance gates for each release milestone.
acceptance_criteria: A single quarterly playbook doc exists with initiative buckets, milestones, owners, and dates
Each milestone has explicit go/no-go criteria and measurable success metrics (timelines, SLOs, acceptance tests)
Security & compliance checklist completed and signed by Security for release candidates
Customer migration/runbook and rollback plan drafted and validated in staging
Compatibility matrix for major on‑prem connectors validated and test coverage added to CI
GTM enablement assets (customer playbook, pricing guidance, enablement training) published to Drive
milestones: M1: Initiative bucketing & prioritization complete — owners assigned (2026-03-22)
M2: Compatibility and capacity gate — tests green on canonical top-5 enterprise topologies (2026-04-30)
M3: Security & KMS integration alpha + customer pilot (2026-05-28)
M4: Upgrade automation and rollback validated in staging (2026-06-10)
M6: Public release window & customer onboarding starts (2026-06-30)
risks: GPU/compute capacity constraints delay Dedicated->Private parity tests
Third-party KMS vendor certification timelines slip
Cross-region networking edge cases uncovered late in QA
Complex customer topologies require >2 integration cycles
Insufficient SRE runbook automation for emergency rollback
mitigations: Reserve dedicated test capacity for top-10 enterprise topologies during Q3
Prioritize vendor certification tasks and escalate with account team
Early-stage chaos/networking simulations to find edge cases before full test matrix runs
Scope hardening: break large integrations into incremental deliverables with canaries
Add emergency rollback automation as a high-priority spike in sprint 1
notes: 2026-02-20: Kickoff with Eng, Security, and Solutions — aligned on three initiative buckets: platform parity, compliance, and customer enablement.
2026-03-01: Engineering flagged a hard dependency on kernel scheduling improvements; added capacity reservation to mitigations.
2026-03-05: Design produced VPC template mocks — pushed to Drive and linked below for review.
2026-03-10: Trade-off discussion: aim for 90-day phased activation vs. single Q3 cutover; decision: phased canary approach to reduce customer risk.
communication_plan: Weekly cross-functional syncs (Tue 11am PT) during prioritization phase
Biweekly tactical workstream check-ins after M2
Stakeholder exec summary decks at M3 and M5
Customer-facing release notes and runbook published 72 hours before activation
